messages.subject: A naive question on .. ~ multi_normal(.. , ..)
parts:
Hello Community,

I am trying to understand how a (1) multivariate normal distribution with 0 correlation can be similar to the use of a  (2) chain of normal distributions

Let's take this input data; 4 observations of 3 normal distributions
          ________________
(P1) - | 1.5 | 2   |  3   |  3.5  |
(P2) - | 15  | 20 |  30 |  40   |
(P3) - | 19  | 20 |  21 |  22   |
          ________________

A hidden parameter of my mix model has the same distribution. So what I can do is:

1) Using a series of normal distributions

value_P1 ~ normal(mean(P1), sd(P1))
value_P2 ~ normal(mean(P2), sd(P2))
value_P3~ normal(mean(P3), sd(P3))

2) Using a multivariate normal distribution with 0 correlation (?)

arr_mean <-   c(mean(P1), mean(P2), mean(P3))
                       __________________________
cov_matrix <-  | sd(P1)^2 | 0             | 0              |
                       | 0             | sd(P2)^2 | 0              |
                       | 0             | 0             | sd(P3)^2  |
                       __________________________

value_vector ~ multi_normal(  mean , cov_matrix )

Why these two cases do not return the same result with generated quantities?

Thanks

messages.author: 7a97c986864bf6d6
messages.subject: Re: A naive question on .. ~ multi_normal(.. , ..)
parts:
Sorry,

actually generated quantities produce the same result, which is much more centered on the mean. I was expecting the generate quantities block to sample from the distribution given, also reproducing the given standard deviations/variances.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] A naive question on .. ~ multi_normal(.. , ..)
parts:
They won't return exactly the same answers because of
the way the randomization works (even with the same seed),
but they should have the same distribution.

But if you do this:

generated quantities {
vector[N] y;
vector[N] z;
z = multi_normal_rng(mu, diag_matrix(sigma .* sigma));
for (n in 1:N)
y[n] = normal_rng(mu[n], sigma[n]);
}

you will get the same distribution over y as over z up to
MCMC error.

- Bob
